Hi Karthik,

Following up from last week's intake call — Aegis Security's assessment team would like to run a short dry run against Redwood's evidence ingestion API before we start the larger SOC2 pen-test next month. The goal is to validate: token scoping, S3 staging + presigned upload, redaction/transformation hooks, and schema validation for artifacts you ingest.

Proposed window: Wed 6/23 09:00-10:30 PT. We'll push a small set of artifacts (sample vuln reports, screenshots, raw pcap snippets) and confirm mapping to your schema.

Quick details: we will POST gzipped JSON and multipart file uploads. Sample filenames will be: pt-results-sample.json, screenshot_01.png, pcap_sample.pcap (we'll only send a truncated pcap for the dry run).

Do we need a dedicated pre-signed bucket or can you provision a short-lived token to your ingestion endpoint? Also please confirm recommended redaction patterns (PII, hostnames) and retention TTL for these trial artifacts.

Attaching a small sample payload to illustrate shape: pt-results-sample.json (no real data).

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz

Aegis Security Assessors

Lena — thanks, this is perfect timing. We can run the dry run on Wed 6/23 09:00-09:45 PT and keep the second half of your window as a contingency. Plan below (high level):

1) Staging: We'll create a short-lived pre-signed S3 bucket scoped to a dry-run prefix (redwood-pt-dryrun/20270623/) and a fallback ingestion endpoint that accepts presigned URLs or direct POSTs.

2) Auth: We'll issue a temporary API key limited to the dry-run prefix, TTL 8 hours. No long-term access will be granted.

3) Schema & redaction: Please map against our Redwood Evidence Schema v2 — attaching for reference (redwood-evidence-schema-v2.json). For the dry run, our default redaction will remove full IP fields and redact any 12+ char hostnames; file-level metadata (filename, size, SHA256) retained.

4) Retention: Dry-run artifacts will be auto-deleted after 7 days. Legal will review if you need shorter retention.

5) Observability: We'll enable request tracing and a per-request token cost/latency log so both teams can correlate.

Next steps:
- Marcus will create the bucket and share presign examples (s3-presign-sample.txt).
- Tessa will run the ingestion test harness and validate the mapping.
- Kimberly, can you confirm whether Redwood's DPA covers short-term test artifacts or if we need a one-off addendum for Aegis?

I've attached the schema and will drop a calendar invite now. If the team prefers, we can add NimbusGRC to the CC for mapping automation.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Partner Integrations, Redwood Inference
